title: Removing bank fees helps immediately, but wider recovery depends on household liquidity
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34993; individual transaction data and large-bank policy changes that eliminated NSF fees or relaxed overdraft policies from 2017-2022
geography: United States; customers of large banks exposed to NSF-fee and overdraft-policy changes

nsf_fees.value: eliminating NSF fees immediately reduced NSF charges across the income distribution

overdraft_fees.value: relaxing overdraft policies reduced overdraft fees mainly for wealthier and more liquid households
overdraft_fees.unit: overdraft-fee response by income and liquidity

later_recovery.value: only the more liquid households later showed declines in late fees, interest payments, account-maintenance fees, and alternative financial-service use such as payday loans

financial_stress.value: the policy changes did not substantially reduce financial stress among more vulnerable households

observations.method: The authors use individual transaction-level data and staggered large-bank policy changes, implementing a stacked event-study estimator to compare elimination of NSF fees and relaxation of overdraft policies.
observations.uncertainty: Account records do not identify every original bill, merchant response, need protected or delayed, family support, affordable-credit option, disability, or household tradeoff. The setting includes multiple treatments and treatment intensities; lower fees do not prove the shortage ended or that a successful payment improved the household month.
observations.subgroup: Customers of large U.S. banks divided by income and liquidity; pay timing, liquid savings, debt, access to family money, affordable credit, and essential bills can differ within those groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A fee reduction can prevent a larger merchant or service loss, and a successful overdraft can be a useful short bridge rather than a harmful cycle. The weaker later effect for vulnerable households may reflect a larger underlying cash gap, not that the policy harmed them.

related_sources.claim: NBER DOI record for Working Paper 34993

boundary: This record adds a liquidity-stratified financial-protection finding: removing a visible fee can be broadly immediate while later recovery differs by household room. It does not establish the original bill, complete household welfare, a universal overdraft effect, or whether payment success prevented or shifted harm.
